summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Lahdo Traitor 1/11)

data.turoyo: Maḥkəyowa, kul gave maḥkəyowa eli w lan naʕime, əmmowa: "Hawxa w hawxa saymiwa appe w qəṭlənwanne w bəʕǧənwanne ba... bu dexono w ba hne, saymiwanne qaflat, qəṭliwanne, məbliwanne.""
data.translation: She used to tell, very often she told me and the other children that they (the Turks and the Kurds) did this and that to them (the Christians), they killed them and choked them with smoke and so on. They used to gather them in qaflat, (groups), took them aWay and killed them.

rationale: First Infectum-wa box; transitive choking by smoke with plural actor and patient.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (Jan 4.I/471)

data.turoyo: Lo m iḏe d l əbʕiwo an nošanək, ann aṯrawoṯanək bʕəǧwolən i marduṯo du ʕamayḏan.
data.translation: It is not because those people did not want to; those countries had torn apart our people's culture.

rationale: New active figurative I.2 and Preterit-wa box; explicit abstract culture theme.

summary: New sense 1: (Detrans.) ersticken, sich erstickt fühlen; fig. vor Kummer oder Ärger ersticken, bedrückt sein

data.gloss: (Detrans.) ersticken, sich erstickt fühlen; fig. vor Kummer oder Ärger ersticken, bedrückt sein

rationale: Supply the absent Detransitive sense list. Existing examples already show emotional distress; new physical contexts show that death is not obligatory. The literal image of bursting versus choking remains an editorial question.

summary: New sense 2: fig. ersticken, unterdrücken (eine Kultur)
rationale: Countries act on i marduṯo du ʕamayḏan. This clear abstract patient contrasts physical strangling; retain the root’s suffocation image rather than importing the machine English tear-apart wording. Single attestation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 41/51)

data.turoyo: Maṭən ann aḥunone lu Kosa, ḥzalle u Kosa taḥt u Bardawil. Omər: "Mudule, bʕəǧleli, hol d qoyamno."
data.translation: Nun kamen die Brüder an und fanden Kôsa unter dem Riesen. »Packt ihn«, rief er, »– er erstickt mich – dass ich aufstehen kann«.

rationale: Thin active Preterit cell; explicit 1sg patient suffix and immediate current distress.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (JTM 3.1/4)

data.translation: Wir alle erstickten (fast), wir krepierten (fast) in den Höhlen.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Preterit cell; plural physical distress in caves, with both repeated tokens quoted once.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 43/24)

data.translation: Da ergrimmte der Minister, erstickte vor Wut und starb.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Preterit cell; canonical long-vowel form and separately asserted death.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (64/282)

data.turoyo: Bʕəǧno mu ṣahwo, kobaʕno maye, d maštatli.
data.translation: Ich vergehe vor Durst, du mußt mir zutrinken geben.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Preterit cell; first-person physical distress with overt m-cause.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (84/43)

data.turoyo: Omər u malko fṣiḥ w fṣiḥ w gaḥəx w mkayafle, bale u malla w i emo bʕiǧi.
data.translation: Der König freute sich und lachte und wurde höchst vergnügt, aber dem Molla und der Mutter wurde es übel zu Mute.

rationale: Brings Detransitive Preterit to five; plural emotional distress without an assertion of death.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (64/78)

data.turoyo: Gidi! Ofaqli, koṯeno, d məbʕəǧno, gmoyaṯno!
data.translation: Mensch, zieh mich heraus! Ich bin am Ersticken, ich werde sterben!

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum cell; literal suffocation distinguished from impending death.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 61/41)

data.turoyo: Ad dədwone kmaḥti ʕal ḥaṣe daš šəšwone, mu qahar kməbʕoǧi aš šəšwone, bu faṣalano d quṭli aš šəšwone.
data.translation: die Fliegen aber setzen sich den Ameisen auf den Rücken, und diese bersten vor Aerger; auf diese Weise töten sie die Ameisen.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum cell; plural emotional use with explicit m-cause and animal participants.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 75/55)

data.turoyo: Alo səmle aʕməx lu qaṭuno, uʕdo məbʕoǧət.
data.translation: warhaftig, der Kater hat bei dir gelegen, mögest du bersten ob deiner Lüge.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum cell; distinct 2sg curse form; preserve edition wording without extracting a lexical lie sense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 2.12/3160)

data.turoyo: Naqla lu Yaḥqub d bə Mirxan lad daboše bʕəǧǧe.
data.translation: Once the bees burst Yaqub of the Mirkhan family.

rationale: Thin active Preterit cell; bees as animal causers and l-coded affected human. Retain machine English burst without diagnosing the event.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.29/4748)

data.turoyo: Kməbʕəǧ darḥal. Awwəl d kmoṭe, kmoḥe u reḥo b qarʕe, kmagəžle, kməbʕəǧ, ḥaša, bayn i pisiye.
data.translation: He suffocates immediately. As soon as he arrives, the smell hits his head, makes him dizzy; he suffocates, with pardon, among the filth.

rationale: Brings Detransitive Infectum to five after round 1; physical smell/filth suffocation and dizziness, not merely emotional distress. Two tokens quoted in one context.

summary: The inherited entry has Detransitive boxes but no numbered Detransitive sense list. Explicit Detransitive 1 now covers physical choking and emotional distress already present in its examples; active sense 1 and all its wording remain unchanged.

Reduced bʕəǧno/bʕəǧina and long-vowel bʕiǧ/bʕiǧina are provisionally grouped together. Identical reduced complaints were inconsistently assigned active Preterit Intransitive and Detransitive by readers; no new active box is established from that inconsistency.

Death is not entailed in all uses: current complaints, projected quoted complaints, and 84/43–50 concern distress, while some narratives add mayəṯ separately. The edition's platzen and ersticken do not by themselves settle the literal physiological image.

Affected subjects occur without an external strangler; m- introduces thirst, heat, smell or emotional cause, and ʕal introduces the occasion of grief at PrS 73/103. These Detransitive events differ from active bʕəǧleli with a patient suffix.
PrS 17/30, 28/29 and 33/30 repeat inherited examples cited under prs 39/37, 70/6 and 83/4; no new quotation is created solely to change numbering.
No light-verb or separately lexicalized idiom was established.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce has no edition translation. English quotations below retain the supplied project machine translation and are marked as such; sense decisions rest on the Turoyo. Where available, round-1 proposals are retained in the human layout and counts, and are not resubmitted in this JSON.
Round 1 already supplies a Detransitive sense and fills its Preterit to five; do not repeat either proposal. Jan adds explicit pit-suffocation support without another emotional sense.

Active bʕəǧǧe has l-coded bees as causers and Yaḥqub as affected participant. The single culture example preserves active l-series coding with an abstract patient and motivates the new figurative sense.
Repeated tokens at 2.12/3160, 2.29/4748 and 4753 retain separate decisions; repetitions are not counted as separate added examples.
Does the livestock use at JTM 1.1/95–96 denote choking, bursting, bloating or more general fatal distress? The supplied German eingehen does not resolve the mechanism.
Confirm whether reduced bʕəǧno/bʕəǧina are Detransitive variants of bʕīǧ, an active intransitive formation or a reduced Infectum. Their common Detransitive filing is provisional.
PrS 31/21: confirm person and mood of bare məbʕəǧ in address to the giant.
Check the PrS citation concordance before altering inherited references.
Can a native speaker distinguish emotional choking from bursting, and confirm which contexts entail death?
At 2.12/3160 does bʕiǧət have second-person -ət despite hano, a different segmentation, or a transcription problem? Preserve the form; no example is based on its person analysis.
What physical outcome is intended in the bee episode: suffocation, bursting, swelling or general severe distress? The supplied machine English does not decide it.
Confirm reduced bʕəǧno at 2.12/3161 in the purpose/result clause; Detransitive Preterit filing follows round 1 provisionally.
Detransitive physiological distress is applied to livestock after excessive salt, thirst and heat. Neither literal bursting, bloating nor a specific veterinary diagnosis can be inferred securely.
Round-1 Detransitive 1 is corroborated by literal suffocation in a pit, with final coffins explicitly showing death in this episode. The verb itself still does not entail death in every use.

Animal causers (bees) enter the active suffocation frame. The adjacent negative Detransitive predicates describe an averted physical outcome, but bursting versus choking versus swelling cannot be resolved medically.
